headline: Six Flags adds seatbelts to Goliath roller coaster following fatal accident
standfirst: Six Flags is installing seatbelts on its Goliath roller coaster in Georgia and conducting safety reviews after a rider fell to his death.
keyPoints: Six Flags is adding seatbelts to the Goliath roller coaster in Georgia.
The change follows the fatal fall of 42-year-old rider Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem.
The park temporarily closed Goliath and eight other rides across five locations following the incident.
An independent review of safety procedures has been commissioned for all company attractions.

paragraphs: Major theme park operator Six Flags has announced plans to install seatbelts on its Goliath roller coaster located in Georgia. This decision comes in the wake of a tragic accident earlier this month when a 42-year-old father and educator named Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was thrown from his seat during operation. The high-speed attraction features an initial 165-foot plunge followed by a second drop of 180 feet, during which the victim fell and collided with other cars on the track.

State authorities in Georgia have launched an active investigation into the circumstances surrounding the fatal incident. In response to the tragedy, Six Flags temporarily closed the Goliath ride along with eight other attractions situated across five different parks within its network. The temporary closures were implemented while initial safety checks and preliminary assessments were carried out by facility personnel.

The company leadership addressed the public on Friday regarding the accident and the subsequent operational halts. Company chief executive John Reilly stated in a written message that the event had deeply affected everyone at the organisation and reaffirmed that safety remains central to their guest experience. Additional seatbelts are scheduled to be placed on other roller coasters across the portfolio that utilise a similar restraint design.

sections.heading: Safety history and industry context
paragraphs: The Goliath attraction at the Georgia facility relies on a lap bar restraint system that locks over the waist of each rider, a mechanism originally designed by manufacturer Bolliger & Mabillard. While lap bars are common across many high-adrenaline amusement park rides globally, this specific tragedy has brought renewed scrutiny to restraint configurations. The company has not yet published a definitive list detailing every specific coaster that will receive the secondary seatbelt retrofits.

Amusement parks operate under strict regulatory frameworks, though oversight varies significantly by region and local jurisdiction. Incidents involving passenger ejections or severe injuries routinely trigger multi-agency inspections and public demands for enhanced preventive measures. Operators frequently find themselves balancing the thrill factor of extreme engineering with the absolute necessity of infallible passenger containment.

sections.heading: Corporate response and external reviews
paragraphs: Alongside the physical modifications being made to the roller coaster fleet, Six Flags has commissioned an independent review of safety procedures for all of its attractions. Chief executive John Reilly acknowledged that rebuilding public confidence requires tangible actions rather than mere statements. The organisation has pledged to maintain open communication regarding its ongoing progress and to hold itself fully accountable to the commitments made to visitors.

This Georgia incident coincides with other legal challenges facing the corporation regarding ride safety at different locations. Court documents show that the company is currently defending itself in a lawsuit concerning alleged bodily harm sustained on the X2 ride at Magic Mountain. That particular ride was permanently shut down by management in September following intense media scrutiny and allegations of negligence.

sections.heading: Broader implications for theme parks
paragraphs: The fatal accident in Georgia serves as a stark reminder of the inherent risks associated with high-velocity amusement park rides. Incidents of this magnitude often prompt industry-wide re-evaluations of safety protocols, restraint standards, and emergency shutdown procedures. Theme park operators must continuously adapt to evolving safety expectations from both regulators and the visiting public to maintain their commercial viability.

Furthermore, legal pressures and negative publicity can significantly impact attendance figures and corporate reputation within the competitive entertainment sector. As independent auditors examine Six Flags procedures, the findings could influence how similar attractions are operated and monitored nationwide. The industry will likely watch these developments closely to see whether secondary restraints become a mandatory standard for high-drop roller coasters.

sections.heading: Moving forward and future oversight
paragraphs: As the Georgia state investigation continues, Six Flags must navigate both regulatory scrutiny and public apprehension before welcoming guests back to the affected rides. The implementation of seatbelts on Goliath represents an immediate operational adjustment designed to address the specific mechanism of the recent failure. Park officials have promised transparency as the independent safety audits progress across their various regional properties.

Ultimately, the success of these new safety initiatives will be measured by their ability to prevent similar tragedies and restore trust among park visitors. The company faces a critical period of operational readjustment as it addresses past legal disputes and implements upgraded mechanical safeguards. Stakeholders across the entertainment industry will monitor these changes to gauge their long-term effectiveness in protecting park guests.

highlight: The company has also commissioned an independent review of the safety procedures for all of its attractions.
socialSummary: Six Flags will add seatbelts to its Goliath roller coaster in Georgia after a rider tragically fell to his death.
